children: South Africa's National Treasury said on Wednesday that Germany and France have committed €300 million ($347.79 million) in concessional financing to support efforts to improve basic municipal services.

The funding, comprising €200 million from Germany's KfW Development Bank and €100 million from France's Agence Française de Développement (AFD), will support the government's Metro Trading Services Reform programme.

The programme covers South Africa's eight metropolitan municipalities, which serve more than 22 million people, and aims to improve the financial and operational performance of electricity, water and sanitation, and waste management services.

Separately, Germany's development cooperation programme, through KfW, has provided a further €350 million in concessional loans to Johannesburg and Cape Town over the past two years to support power grid upgrades and renewable energy integration.
